The '''2022–23 Texas Longhorns men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Texas at Austin]] in the [[2022–23 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. They were led by interim head coach [[Rodney Terry]] and played their home games at the [[Moody Center]] in [[Austin, Texas]] as members of the [[Big 12 Conference]]. The Longhorns played at the newly-built [[Moody Center]] after playing at [[Frank Erwin Center]] for 45 years.<ref>{{cite news|last=Espey Bo|url=https://thedailytexan.com/2022/02/28/looking-back-top-moments-at-the-drum-frank-erwin-center-texas/|work=The Daily Texan|title= Looking Back: Top moments at The Drum|date=February 28, 2022|accessdate=March 15, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Aldridge Olivia|url=https://communityimpact.com/austin/central-austin/development/2021/04/28/inside-look-moody-center-scheduled-to-open-in-april-2022/|work=Community Impact Newspaper|title=Inside look: Moody Center scheduled to open in April 2022|date=April 28, 2021|accessdate=March 15, 2022}}</ref> They finished the season 23–8, 12–6 in Big 12 play to finish in second place. As the No. 2 seed in the [[2023 Big 12 men's basketball tournament|Big 12 tournament]], they defeated [[2022–23 Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball team|Oklahoma State]], [[2022–23 TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball team|TCU]], and top-seeded [[2022–23 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|Kansas]] to win the tournament. They received an automatic bid to the [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 2 seed in the Midwest Region, where they defeated [[2022–23 Colgate Raiders men's basketball team|Colgate]], [[2022–23 Penn State Nittany Lions basketball team|Penn State]], and [[2022–23 Xavier Musketeers men's basketball team|Xavier]] to reach the Elite Eight, their first appearance since [[2008 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2008]]. There, the Longhorns finally fell to [[2022–23 Miami Hurricanes men's basketball team|Miami (FL)]], bringing their season to a close with a final record of 29–9.

On December 12, 2022, head coach [[Chris Beard (basketball)|Chris Beard]] was suspended without pay after an early morning arrest for third-degree felony domestic assault on his fiancée.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/35240809/texas-suspends-coach-chris-beard-arrest-assault-charge|title=Texas suspends coach Chris Beard after arrest on assault charge|accessdate=January 5, 2023}}</ref> Associate head coach [[Rodney Terry]] began serving as acting head coach starting with the December 12th game versus [[2022–23 Rice Owls men's basketball team|Rice]].

On January 5, 2023, Beard was officially terminated by Texas athletic director [[Chris Del Conte]]; Terry continued as acting head coach for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://texassports.com/news/2023/1/5/mens-basketball-statement-from-university-of-texas-vice-president-and-athletics-director-chris-del-conte.aspx|title=Statement from University of Texas Vice President and Athletics Director Chris Del Conte|accessdate=January 5, 2023}}</ref> On March 27, 2023, Terry was named the permanent full-time head coach for the Longhorns following their impressive run to the Elite Eight in the 2023 NCAA tournament.<ref>{{cite web |title=Rodney Terry named Men's Basketball head coach |url=https://texassports.com/news/2023/3/28/rodney-terry-named-mens-basketball-head-coach.aspx |website=Texas Sports |publisher=University of Texas Athletics |access-date=2 April 2023}}</ref>

==Previous season==

===Season outlook===
Heading into the [[2021–22 Texas Longhorns men's basketball team|2021–22]] season, there was a lot of excitement surrounding the program after the hiring of former [[Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball|Texas Tech]] head coach [[Chris Beard (basketball)|Chris Beard]]. Texas came into the season ranked number 5 in both the [[2021–22 NCAA Division I men's basketball rankings|AP Preseason Poll]] and the [[Coaches Poll|USA Today Coaches Poll]], further invigorating the hype.<ref>{{cite news|last=Davis Brian|url=https://www.hookem.com/story/sports/mens-basketball/2021/10/18/texas-basketball-jumps-no-5-ap-top-25-preseason-poll/8510854002/|work=Hookem|title=After Chris Beard’s busy offseason of recruiting, Texas jumps to No. 5 in AP Top 25 preseason poll|date=October 18, 2021|accessdate= March 15, 2022}}</ref> Also, there was a lot of roster turnover heading into the season with Beard landing 6 of the top 31 transfers in the transfer portal, and only 1 high school recruit in Jaylon Tyson.<ref>{{cite news|last=Borba Kevin|url=https://longhornswire.usatoday.com/lists/texas-longhorns-basketball-chris-beard-top-transfers-roster-2021-outlook-recruiting-commitment/|work=Longhorns Wire|title=Texas Basketball: Chris Beard has landed six of the top 31 transfers|date=July 18, 2021|accessdate= March 15, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=|url=https://247sports.com/college/texas/Season/2021-Basketball/Commits/|work=247 Sports|title=Texas 2021 Basketball Commits|date=|accessdate= March 15, 2022}}</ref> In Beard's inaugural season, The Longhorns finished the 2021–22 season at 21–11.<ref>{{cite news|last=|url=https://texassports.com/sports/mens-basketball/schedule|work=Texas Sports|title=2021-22 Men's Basketball Schedule|date=|accessdate=}}</ref> During the regular season, Texas finished with a record of 21–10, 10–8 in conference play, and 11–2 in non-conference play. Furthermore, the Longhorns were 3–8 against top-25 competition. Texas went 16–3 at home, 4–7 on the road, and 1–1 at neutral sites.<ref>{{cite news|last=|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/schools/texas/2022.html|work=Sports Reference|title=2021-22 Texas Longhorns Roster and Stats|date=|accessdate= March 15, 2022}}</ref> This was the Longhorns first 20-win season since the [[2018–19 Texas Longhorns men's basketball team|2018-19]] season, they went 21–16 that year. However, the season did have its ups and downs. Additionally, Jaylon Tyson and [[Tre Mitchell]] suddenly departed the team mid-season, and Texas lost their last 2 games of the regular season with an early exit in the Big 12 tournament, being eliminated in the first round by TCU 60–65.<ref>{{cite news|last=Galatzan Matt|url=https://www.si.com/college/texas/news/longhorns-chris-beard-tre-mitchell-leave-of-absence|work=SI|title=Longhorns Big Man Tre Mitchell Takes Indefinite Leave Of Absence|date=February 15, 2022|accessdate= March 15, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Eberts Wescott|url=https://www.burntorangenation.com/2021/12/27/22855772/jaylon-tyson-enters-ncaa-transfer-portal-texas-longhorns|work=Burnt Orange Nation|title=Texas F Jaylon Tyson enters the NCAA transfer portal|date=December 27, 2021|accessdate= March 15, 2022}}</ref>

===Big 12 tournament===
Texas entered the Big 12 tournament as a 4-seed.<ref>{{cite news|last=Parker Cameron|url=https://www.burntorangenation.com/2022/3/5/22963666/texas-longhorns-tcu-horned-forgs-big-12-tournament-game-time-television-bracket|work=Burnt Orange Nation|title=Texas claims No. 4 seed, opens Big 12 tournament against TCU|date=March 5, 2022|accessdate= March 15, 2022}}</ref> They faced off against 5-seed [[2021–22 TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball team|TCU]] where they were defeated 60–65, giving them a 6-seed heading into the [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]].<ref>{{cite news|last=|url=https://texassports.com/sports/mens-basketball/stats/2021-22/tcu/boxscore/14855|work=Texas Sports|title=Box Score vs. TCU|date=|accessdate=}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Daniel Cody|url=https://www.burntorangenation.com/basketball/2022/3/13/22975359/texas-longhorns-6-seed-ncaa-tournament-march-madness-virginia-tech-hokies|work=Burnt Orange Nation|title=Texas earns No. 6 seed in NCAA tournament, will face Virginia Tech|date=March 13, 2022|accessdate= March 15, 2022}}</ref>

===NCAA tournament===
Texas entered the NCAA tournament as a 6-seed, facing off against 11-seed [[2021–22 Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball team|Virginia Tech]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Chute Nate|url=https://www.statesman.com/story/sports/2022/03/13/texas-virginia-tech-prediction-march-madness-upset-odds-6-11-seed-ncaa-tournament-basketball/9452789002/|work=Austin American-Statesman|title=How many times has No. 11 seed beat a No. 6? A look at the odds of a Virginia Tech upset over Texas|date=March 13, 2022|accessdate=March 15, 2022}}</ref> Against Virginia Tech, Texas won 81–73.<ref>{{cite news|last=|url=https://texassports.com/sports/mens-basketball/stats/2021-22/virginia-tech/boxscore/14867|work=Texas Sports|title=Box Score vs. Virginia Tech|date=March 18, 2022|accessdate=March 21, 2022}}</ref> Furthermore, Texas's victory against Virginia Tech marked their first win in the NCAA tournament since 2014.<ref>{{cite news|last=|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/gametracker/recap/NCAAB_20220318_VATECH@TEXAS/|work=CBS Sports|title=Texas beats Hokies 81-73 for 1st NCAA tourney win since 2014|date=March 18, 2022|accessdate=March 21, 2022}}</ref> In the round of 32, Texas faced off against 3-seed Purdue losing 71–81, ending their season.<ref>{{cite news|last=Carmin Mike|url=https://www.jconline.com/story/sports/college/purdue/basketball/2022/03/20/march-madness-purdue-sweet-16-bound-after-taking-down-texas/7103138001/|work=Journal & Courier|title=March Madness: Purdue 81, Texas 71 - How it happened, what it means, what's next|date=March 20, 2022|accessdate=March 22, 2022}}</ref>
